description.overview: What you are subscribed to, what it has cost, and how much is left.
description.keys: The gateway keys you hold. What a key is bound to is decided when it is minted and never taken from a request header.
description.models: The names you can address on this instance, and which of them your permission rules allow.
description.usage: Your own requests, tokens and cost over a window.
description.quota: The budget windows your requests are charged against, from your key up to your organization.
description.requests: Your last fifty requests, without bodies, headers or addresses.
description.account: Your password, your scopes, the sessions you have open and the programs you have authorized.
description.users: Gateway accounts. A password is write-only: a user reports whether it has one, never what it is.
description.api-keys: Every key on this instance. The plaintext exists at the mint and at a rotation, and nowhere else unless the row retained it.
description.organizations: The outer scope that owns teams and shared credentials.
description.teams: An inner scope inside exactly one organization. A team cannot be moved between them.
description.permissions: What one subject may ask of which provider, model and operation. Higher priority wins; a deny beats an allow.
description.rate-limits: What to count and how far. The live counters are in the cache; these are the rows that configure them.
description.plans: Downstream plans and the pool that backs them.
description.plan-limits: A plan's per-window allowances, in USD.
description.subscriptions: One user's issued subscription to a plan.
description.pools: Capacity pools and the upstream subscriptions behind them.
description.pool-members: The credentials a pool draws on, deduplicated by source key.
description.oauth-clients: Registered public clients. This registry issues no client secrets, so nothing here is secret.
description.sessions: Live console and portal sign-ins. A session can be listed and ended, never read back.
description.audit: Every write somebody made. Reads are not audited, because a trail that is mostly `list` is a trail nobody reads.
